ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, point $O$ is the origin. The line $BC$ intersects the y-axis at point $B$ and the x-axis at point $C$. The coordinates of point $B$ are $(0,4)$, and $OB=OC$. What is the analytical expression of line $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $B(0, 4)$, \\
it follows that $OB=4$, \\
thus $OC=OB=4$, \\
implying $C(4, 0)$ \\
Let the equation of line $BC$ be $y=kx+b\ (k \neq 0)$, \\
therefore $\left\{\begin{array}{l}b = 4 \\ 4k + b = 0 \end{array}\right.$ \\
hence $\left\{\begin{array}{l}k = -1 \\ b = 4 \end{array}\right.$ \\
Thus, the equation of line $BC$ is $y = -x + 4$, so the answer is \boxed{y = -x + 4}.
